title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is an impersonation fraud carried out through a synthetic video call. The face and voice of a public figure were generated to lend authority to a request for money, and the request was then escalated through a sequence of invented fees. The AI component sat at the front of the scheme, establishing enough credibility for the victim to keep paying.

The failure occurred at the point of contact between a member of the public and an unverified caller on a consumer messaging app. Nothing in the deployment verified that the person on the call was who he appeared to be, and the victim had no independent channel to confirm the offer. Catching it would have required either provenance signals on the synthetic media itself or a verification step outside the call, such as contacting the Chief Minister's office directly. Neither was in place.

What is not established is who produced the deepfake, whether anyone has been charged, or whether the case has progressed beyond registration. The police registered a case under the Information Technology Act, and that registration is not a finding of guilt against any person.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A 29-year-old security guard in Bengaluru named Ratikanta Giri received a WhatsApp video call on September 9 from someone using an AI-generated deepfake of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay. The caller offered him Rs 11 lakh in financial aid, then had a supposed manager demand fees for exchange charges, a locked PIN, and a fake CBI fine. Giri paid over Rs 1.04 lakh through a digital payment app before refusing a further Rs 50,000 demand and realizing he had been cheated.

Giri contacted the cybercrime helpline 1930 and then approached Byappanahalli police, who registered a case under the Information Technology Act. This is the first such deepfake case reported in the city. Fraudsters had sent him a letter claiming Rs 5 lakh was allotted to him and identity proof of a supposed CBI officer. A senior officer urged people not to believe such calls or make payments based on them.
